subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview exempt reference-shaped assignment values globally, or restrict that exemption to code contexts where they are unambiguously identifiers or member expressions?
rationale: The reported behavior is a real false positive, but the scanner processes mixed-language bundle text; a global regex exemption could weaken detection outside TypeScript and requires an explicit safety-boundary choice.

options.title: Use context-aware references
options.body: Recognize identifiers and member expressions only in supported code contexts and retain conservative scanning for ambiguous configuration text.

options.title: Allow all reference shapes
options.body: Treat every pure identifier or dotted member expression as safe across bundle text, accepting the wider false-negative risk for simpler implementation.

recommendation.title: Use context-aware references
recommendation.body: Recognize identifiers and member expressions only in supported code contexts and retain conservative scanning for ambiguous configuration text.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent scanner-hardening work and its fail-closed policy are concentrated in this contributor’s merged changes.
